newsitem.title: INDIA: Highlights of Parliament session - July 30.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Parliament session - July 30.

text.p: Following are highlights of debates in India's Parliament on Wednesday, July 30 --
** Home minister Indrajit Gupta ruled out the possibility of Maharashtra coming under President's Rule.
"As of today the situation does not warrant imposition of President's Rule in Maharashtra," Gupta told the Rajya Sabha, the upper house of parliament.
He said he regretted that prominent people including lawmakers had been reportedly involved in attacking the residence of the leader of opposition in the state assembly Chhagan Bhujbal.

Gupta said he hoped the judicial commission probing the police firing and other violent incidents in the aftermath of desecration of B.R. Ambedkar's statue in Bombay recently would issue objective findings soon.
Gupta told the lawmakers that Shiv Sena supremo Bal Thackarey, while regetting the attack, had promised that such incidents would not recur. He said New Delhi would not ignore any repetitions.
The Home Minister said the need of the hour was to ponder over how to save the country from the clutches of the corrupt and criminals.
He said a committee of members of parliament may go into the issue of dealing with the situation arising out of the incident of desecration of the statue of Ambedkar.
Earlier Congress and Shiv Sena lawmakers traded angry charges against one another.
Trouble broke out when Shiv Sena member Sanja Nirupam tore up a newspaper clipping which Congress MP Govindrao Adik was trying to display.

The debate on the Maharashtra issue was inconclusive and the reply is expected to come on Thursday on the motion moved by the Congress leader of the house that "This house expresses its deep concern over the atrocities committed on Dalits in Mumbai (Bombay), Nagpur and other places in the state of Maharashtra and in other parts of the country."

Shiv Sena leader in the lower house, Madhukar Sirpotdar alleged that the Congress was trying to project itself as a champion of the Dalits and it would be unfair to paint the Shiv Sena as as anti-Dalit. "We are well wishers of the Dalits," he said while maintaining that the state had been saved from disastor because of the effective rule of the Shiv Sena and BJP combine.
The Shiv Sena-BJP alliance was providing the most stable government in Maharashtra, he insisted.

** Earlier during the zero hour in the Lok Sabha loud arguments broke out between Samajwadi party members and the Bharatiya Janata Party deputies over the issue of land compensation to the villagers of Dabrala in Badayun district of the northern state of Uttar Pradesh.

** Ramesh Chenithala of Congress demanded the government must take immediate action to save the rubber growers of Kerala. He said that although the price of rubber has come down to 30 rupees per kg, the Centre had not heeded appeals from the state government to arrest the falling trend.

Raising the issue during zero hour, Chenithala, who was supported by P.C. Thomas, said that the State Trading Corporation had also not intervened to save the situation. He urged the STC to immediately procure at least 25,000 tonnes of rubber.

** The Rajya Sabha was later adjourned for the day ahead of schedule as members from all parties pressed the acting chairperson Saroj Khaparde to take up the debate on the Bihar situation on Thursday.
